title: The Heart and Circulation (KS4 Biology)
subject: Biology
strapline: The double pump and the three types of blood vessel.
facts: Humans have a double circulatory system: one loop to the lungs, one to the rest of the body.
The heart has four chambers: right and left atria (top) and right and left ventricles (bottom).
The right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs; the left side pumps oxygenated blood to the body.
The left ventricle has a thicker muscular wall because it pumps blood all round the body.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure and have thick, elastic walls.
Veins carry blood back to the heart at low pressure and have valves to stop backflow.
Capillaries are one cell thick, allowing exchange of substances (oxygen, glucose, CO₂) with cells.

quick_quiz.q: Why is the left ventricle wall thicker than the right?
quick_quiz.a: it pumps blood all around the body (higher pressure)

quick_quiz.q: Which vessel carries blood away from the heart?
What feature in veins prevents backflow?

teacher_tips: Remember "ventricles pump out" and left = to the body.
